summary_plain: Moves about 49 arcseconds per hour across 20 images over 13.1 hours. It matches the known asteroid 2399 Terradas (1971 MA).

orbit.reported_orbit: The arc is too short to fix one orbit, so this is the most circular of the 717 sampled orbits that fit the detections; the clones show the range.

known_object.observer: SPHEREx (geocentric JPL predictions corrected with the spacecraft position from the FITS headers)

scores.definition: Rule-based ranking score in [0, 1]: motion_consistency x snr x (1 - artifact_likelihood). It orders candidates for review. It is not a probability.

explanation.text: Detected in 20 SPHEREx exposures spanning 13.1 hours. It moves 49.1 arcseconds per hour toward position angle 76 degrees. A straight-line motion plus orbital-parallax fit leaves 0.70 arcseconds of scatter. SPHEREx's own orbital parallax puts it roughly 1.55 AU away (range 1.06 to 2.87 AU). Its faintest detection has a signal-to-noise ratio of 5.5. Its positions match JPL's prediction for 2399 Terradas (1971 MA) to within 1.2 arcseconds at every epoch.
